answer: The admission burn is multiplied by 16 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. The terrace multiplier is published, charged in mesa, and harbor lists each payment. A burst of registrations hence prices itself out, because the marginal alias burns more than the first by design. A farm of 1379 identities would post 2422 proofs and burn roughly 11 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
